description: Deliverable 2: 'money you could have saved' counterfactual vs the basic-service rate, supply portion only, default 6-month period. Given actual monthly kWh and the competitive supply rate the household paid, compute what basic service would have cost and the SIGNED savings (positive = saved, negative = overpaid). Builds data/build/savings_model.json with a worked-example set. Depends on FEAT-001's load_fixed_rates() and the term-span helper.
steps: Add a term_spans() helper (in src/backend/data_sources.py or savings_model.py) mirroring reference/ingest_rates.py `derive_terms`: per utility, term start = previous term end + 1 month, fixed value sits on the term's LAST month; map a calendar month to the fixed rate of the term covering it. Column->UtilityId NG->NG, NSTAR->EV_EAST, WMECo->EV_WEST, Unitil->UNITIL.

Create src/backend/savings_model.py with a pure function savings(kwh_by_month, user_rate_cents, utility, start_ym, months=6) computing per-month userMonthly = user_rate_cents*kWh/100, defaultMonthly = basicServiceCents*kWh/100, savedMonthly = (basicServiceCents - user_rate_cents)*kWh/100 (+ = saved, - = overpaid), and savedTotal = sum. Internal math unrounded; also return display strings half-up to cents matching ^-?\$\d{1,3}(,\d{3})*\.\d{2}$.

Create src/backend/build_savings.py entrypoint that writes data/build/savings_model.json per the plan shape (keys: generated, method, defaultPeriodMonths=6, basicServiceRatesCents{NG,EV_EAST,EV_WEST,UNITIL,term}, examples[]). Include at least the two worked examples from the plan (the overpaid NG 22.0c case and a positive-savings case). Print a one-line summary.
Create tests/backend/test_savings.py covering tests 4-6 from the plan.
acceptance_criteria: Running `python3 src/backend/build_savings.py` creates/overwrites data/build/savings_model.json with no error.

Hand-worked case: NG, userRate 22.0c, basic 17.185c, 650 kWh, 6 months => savedTotal == -187.785 (within 1e-9) and display '-$187.79'; positive case userRate 15.0c vs NG 17.185c, 600 kWh, 1 month => +13.11 / '+$13.11' (or '$13.11').
userRate == basic => saved == 0; savings linear in kWh (within 1e-9); 6-month total == sum of the 6 monthly values exactly.
Basic-service rate selected for Aug 2026-Jan 2027 equals NG 17.185, EV_EAST 17.323, EV_WEST 15.934, UNITIL 18.921.
Running `python3 -m pytest tests/backend/test_savings.py -q` passes all tests.
findings: Implemented in src/backend/savings_model.py (pure functions) + src/backend/build_savings.py (entrypoint), tests in tests/backend/test_savings.py. term_spans() lives in savings_model.py (NOT data_sources.py) to avoid touching FEAT-001's file; it mirrors ingest_rates.derive_terms (start = prev end + 1 month, value on term's LAST month). Public API for later steps/FEAT: savings_model.savings(kwh_by_month, user_rate_cents, utility, start_ym, months=6), basic_service_cents(utility, year, month, spans=None), term_spans(fixed_rows=None). Utility ids: NG, EV_EAST, EV_WEST, UNITIL. Display is half-up to cents via Decimal ROUND_HALF_UP and emits regex-matching '$13.11' (no leading '+') for positive values, '-$187.79' for negative; matches ^-?\$\d{1,3}(,\d{3})*\.\d{2}$. Default window Aug 2026-Jan 2027 (current fixed term): NG 17.185, EV_EAST 17.323, EV_WEST 15.934, UNITIL 18.921. Artifact data/build/savings_model.json written with sorted keys + trailing newline (keys: basicServiceRatesCents{..,term}, defaultPeriodMonths=6, examples[2], generated, method). Hand-worked checks pass: overpaid NG 22.0c/650kWh/6mo -> savedTotal -187.785 / '-$187.79'; positive NG 15.0c/600kWh/1mo -> +13.11 / '$13.11'. Verification: build entrypoint ran clean, test_savings.py 11 passed, full tests/backend 26 passed, reference G-DATA-3 still PASS.
